notes: Dispute over water-meter rates for an apartment house's café/bar/garage under the city charter; no bearing on letting rooms/dwellings or its regulation.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
notes: Election-of-remedies dispute between landlord and long-term tenant (ejectment vs. summary nonpayment proceeding); no lodging/short-term letting issue.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: Where a furnished house is let for a short season for immediate occupation, the law implies a warranty that the furniture is clean and fit for use; because the beds and furniture were overrun with vermin on the tenant's entry, he was justified in abandoning the premises, and judgment for the landlord's rent claim was reversed for new trial.

quotes.text: I find no decision in this state which repudiates what appears to be the English rule, that in the case of a lease of a furnished house, particularly one for a short season or under other circumstances which indicate the purpose of immediate occupancy, there is implied a warranty of the availabilty of the furniture.
Under these circumstances, there was an implied warranty that the furniture at least was clean and suitable for use.
I think that the evidence sufficiently established a situation warranting the abandonment of the premises by defendant

notes: Lease of a furnished Long Island house for the winter season (Oct.-May); court treats short-season furnished letting as a distinct category warranting an implied warranty of tenantability, protecting the tenant. Record is unclear whether plaintiff-lessor was a householder letting his own house or a rental operator, so who_was_letting left unclear.

notes: Liability-insurance coverage dispute over roof repairs and a warranty that premises were 'occupied as Apartment Hotel'; the apartment-hotel label is only an insurance term, not a ruling on letting/lodging practice.
Partition action; receiver of rents seeks instructions on collecting rent/use-and-occupation from a co-tenant with dower rights occupying the family home. No compensated lodger/boarder arrangement.
Enforcement of a deed covenant restricting lots to residential-only buildings against construction of a business block; no letting or lodging of rooms at issue.

court: County Court of New York, Oneida County
notes: Dispute over validity of a lease-renewal endorsement following a trust-deed conveyance of the fee; ordinary commercial lease/trust title question, not lodging or short-term letting.

Mandamus to compel issuance of a moving-picture-show license under Buffalo's zoning/licensing ordinance; unrelated to dwelling/room letting.

Occupancy was incident to a master-servant employment contract, not a paid lodger/tenant arrangement; addresses when service-occupancy terminates for summary removal, a distinct doctrine from compensated short-term letting.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
notes: Ordinary $12/month apartment tenancy; dispute is whether tenant could set off a bank deposit against rent following the landlord's bank failure/bankruptcy, turning on classification of the tenancy as monthly. No lodging-house or short-let characterization issue.

Breach-of-covenant-for-quiet-enjoyment action arising from a 21-year commercial ground lease and prior vexatious ejectment/dispossess suits; not a lodging/short-term letting case.

Conditional-sale-of-furniture dispute under the Personal Property Law; plaintiff's employment 'running a rooming-house' is mentioned only in passing as background, not adjudicated.

notes: Rent-arrears action turning on whether a mortgage-foreclosure holdover tenancy was monthly or an indefinite hiring under Real Property Law §232; ordinary commercial tenancy, not lodging.
Dispute over an oil-drilling lease/option and ownership of oil wells; unrelated to dwelling/room letting.
